decisions.reason: As a recent extension of the firm's core coolant-management line, it is close to existing capabilities and customer needs, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it while results are still forming.

The centrifuge fits the firm's filtration and sustainability positioning, and in a growing industry a large firm with R&D slack would usually give such an adjacent product more time before considering withdrawal.
Coolant nozzles are a small, complementary add-on to the established offer, so the cost of carrying them is low and their portfolio value makes removal unlikely.

Although only close to rather than fully within the established offer, the scraper belt chip conveyor still matches the firm's automation and material-flow business, so management would likely keep it unless clear shortfalls emerged.
This product builds directly on the firm's chip-handling portfolio and supports modular system selling, which makes it likely to stay on the market while adoption develops.

The hinged belt chip conveyor is somewhat more exposed to overlap and comparison within the firm's broad conveyor range, but organizational slack and strategic fit still make retention more likely than withdrawal.
